title: Day 687 — Federal Operation Against CJNG's "Tío Lako" Cell Sparks Michoacán Narco-Blockades
detail: On August 19, 2026 (Day 687, Wednesday), President Sheinbaum confirmed at her mañanera an active federal operation to detain "one or several priority objectives" in Michoacán, with the Security Cabinet to brief details later that day. Army-led raids in Tanhuato and Ecuandureo targeted a CJNG cell run by regional plaza boss Heraclio Guerrero Martínez, alias "Tío Lako"; he evaded capture, but 9 people were detained, including his daughter Marisol "N" and partner Lourdes "N." The operation triggered more than 20 narco-blockades and vehicle burnings on highways across Zamora, La Piedad, Ecuandureo, Zacapu, Chilchota and Tangancícuaro, and an armed clash left a preliminary 5 civilians dead. Officials tied the crackdown to Tío Lako's alleged orders to attack National Guard troops after the February 22, 2026 SEDENA operation in Tapalpa, Jalisco that killed CJNG leader Rubén "El Mencho" Oseguera Cervantes and Tío Lako's own son, Rubén "El R1" Guerrero Valadez.

media.caption: Federal operation against Tío Lako's CJNG cell in Michoacán triggers narco-blockades

title: Day 687 — Sheinbaum Calls Detained Argentine Strategist Cerimedo a "Feminicida," Accuses La Derecha Diario of Running Bot Network
detail: On August 19, 2026 (Day 687, Wednesday), President Sheinbaum reacted to the August 18 detention in Bolivia of Argentine right-wing strategist Fernando Cerimedo — a former adviser to Javier Milei and founder of La Derecha Diario — after his ex-wife Nadia Beller accused him of hiring hitmen to attempt to kill her while she was pregnant; Bolivian prosecutors sought 180 days of preventive detention. Sheinbaum said Cerimedo was "a feminicida, in short words, who attacked his wife multiple times," and separately accused La Derecha Diario of amplifying attacks on her government through a bot network, describing it as part of a coordinated international right-wing media operation.

media.caption: Sheinbaum calls Fernando Cerimedo a "feminicida" and accuses La Derecha Diario of running a bot network

title: Day 687 — Sheinbaum Unveils 147B-Peso PODECOBI Industrial Pole in Zapotlán, Hidalgo
detail: On August 19, 2026 (Day 687, Wednesday), President Sheinbaum and Hidalgo Governor Julio Menchaca presented the PODECOBI (Polo de Desarrollo Económico para el Bienestar) industrial pole in Zapotlán: 130 projects worth 147 billion pesos across 910 hectares, projected to create 191,000 jobs in manufacturing, logistics, pharmaceuticals and medical devices. Lead investors include DEWA Capital (10.1 billion pesos for an industrial complex, ~5,100 jobs in its initial phase) and Cooperativa Cruz Azul (6.5 billion pesos to expand cement production and modernize hospital infrastructure in nearby Tula, ~14,200 jobs).

media.caption: Sheinbaum and Hidalgo Gov. Julio Menchaca unveil the 147-billion-peso PODECOBI industrial pole in Zapotlán

title: Day 687 — Sheinbaum Presses UNAM to Expand Admissions, Cites Budget Reallocation
detail: On August 19, 2026 (Day 687, Wednesday), President Sheinbaum called on UNAM to open more admission spots for applicants it turns away each cycle, saying the university has the resources to do so by "simply reorienting the budget," and said a scheme for students not admitted would be presented the following Monday (Aug 24). She pointed to the "Mi Derecho, Mi Lugar" program and alternative institutions — Universidad Rosario Castellanos and Universidad Benito Juárez — as already easing the bottleneck, noting their graduates now receive accredited higher-education certification.

media.caption: Sheinbaum calls on UNAM to expand admissions by reorienting its budget
